title: Stay, or review for exit?
objectives: Read the five signals and what each usually means.
Know what to set out before any exit.
body_md:
| Signal | Usually means |
|---|---|
| Lagging benchmark for 1 year, process unchanged, style out of favour | Stay; explain the style cycle |
| Lagging benchmark and peers for 3+ years | Review for exit |
| Fund manager or key team leaves | Review immediately |
| Style drift away from what was sold | Review; it is no longer the product the client bought |
| Client's goal, horizon or liquidity need changes | Re-check suitability; may reduce |

Before any exit, set out the exit load, the tax on gains, and the cost of rebuilding elsewhere.

> **Investor takeaway:** Judge a PMS on 3+ years of after-fee returns vs its benchmark, not on one quarter.
example: The star manager leaves. You inform the client the same day, explain the review process, and set a date to compare the new team's process against what was sold. No automatic exit.
say: The manager and process are unchanged, so we stay.
Before any exit, here is the exit load, the tax and the cost of rebuilding elsewhere.
never: Exit now, before it gets worse.

check.q: A PMS lagged its benchmark for 1 year; process unchanged, style out of favour. Action?
o: Stay, and explain the style cycle
Switch to last year's top PMS
check.why: Review for exit only after 3+ years behind benchmark AND peers.

check.q: The star fund manager has just left the PMS firm. What should you do?
o: Say nothing unless the client asks
Review immediately and inform the client proactively
check.why: No panic and no automatic exit, but an immediate review.

check.q: Before recommending any PMS exit, what must you set out?
o: Exit load, tax on gains and the cost of rebuilding elsewhere
check.why: Exiting has real costs in a PMS, because tax falls in the client's own hands.
